parameters.query:
select ticker
from universe
where type = 'Common Stock'

BEGIN;

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Retire redundant tickers -- FLAG, DO NOT DELETE.  (rewritten 2026-09-25)
--
-- WHY THE DELETE HAD TO GO. The old body looped every public table with a ticker/symbol
-- column and deleted the missing names, then deleted them from universe. That is why the
-- price record is survivor-only: 0 of 6,423 tickers in daily_prices lack a universe row, so
-- nothing that ever delisted kept its history. A 15-year backfill loaded into that regime is
-- maximally survivor-biased the day it completes -- and the rows being erased are exactly the
-- ones the ranking model's bottom decile is meant to learn from: stocks on the way to zero.
--
-- WHY IT IS DATA-DRIVEN, not payload-driven. Two things were checked before writing this:
--   * universe.miss_count is 0 for all 5,594 common stocks -- nothing maintains it, so a rule
--     keyed on "miss_count >= 3" would never fire;
--   * of the 35 tickers currently flagged is_delisted, 30 are still trading -- the existing
--     flags are simply wrong.
-- Staleness is therefore derived from daily_prices: a ticker the market is still pricing is
-- live, whatever any counter or previous flag says. That self-heals those 30 on the first run.
--
-- WHAT RETIREMENT MEANS NOW: universe.is_delisted = true, nothing deleted. Nothing downstream
-- needs cleaning -- the price-driven objects (mv_relative_strength, mv_dtrend_hist,
-- prebreakout, ML scoring) are date-anchored and drop a name with no recent bars on their own,
-- and the fundamentals layer (v_fund_metrics, v_eval_*, mv_fund_metrics) already filters
-- is_delisted.
--
-- REQUIRED COMPANION CHANGE, or this saves nothing (dead names keep being requested daily):
--   MyCurrentUniverse  ->  select ticker from universe
--                          where type = 'Common Stock'
--                            and coalesce(is_delisted, false) = false
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- The loader's own missing list, kept only for the diagnostic at the end: it is a same-day
-- signal where price staleness needs the grace window to elapse.
create temp table _del(ticker text primary key) on commit drop;

insert into _del(ticker)
select distinct trim(v->>'ticker')
from json_array_elements($JSON$ {{ JSON.stringify($input.all().map(i => i.json)) }} $JSON$::json) v
where nullif(trim(v->>'ticker'),'') is not null;

-- Staleness in the MARKET's own sessions, not calendar days, so a long weekend or a missed
-- load cannot retire anything. Grouped aggregate, not a per-ticker subquery: the correlated
-- form takes >30s against 6.8M rows, this runs in ~0.6s.
create temp table _stale on commit drop as
with mkt as (
  select date, row_number() over (order by date desc) as sessions_ago
  from (select distinct date from daily_prices where date > current_date - 90) d),
lastbar as (
  select p.ticker, max(p.date) as last_date
  from daily_prices p
  where p.date > current_date - 120
  group by p.ticker)
select u.ticker,
       lb.last_date,
       coalesce(m.sessions_ago, 999) as sessions_since
from universe u
left join lastbar lb on lb.ticker = u.ticker
left join mkt m on m.date = lb.last_date
where u.type = 'Common Stock';

do $$
declare
  grace_sessions int := 10;    -- ~2 weeks of trading with no print before a name is retired
  n_retired bigint; n_restored bigint; n_warning bigint; n_missing bigint;
begin
  -- 1. RETIRE: the market has traded for grace_sessions sessions and this name has not printed.
  update universe u
     set is_delisted = true,
         miss_count  = s.sessions_since,      -- finally gives the column a meaning
         updated_at  = now()
    from _stale s
   where u.ticker = s.ticker
     and coalesce(u.is_delisted, false) = false
     and s.sessions_since >= grace_sessions;
  get diagnostics n_retired = row_count;

  -- 2. RESTORE: printing again (halt lifted, re-listing, or the flag was simply wrong).
  --    This is what corrects the 30 flagged names that never stopped trading.
  update universe u
     set is_delisted = false,
         miss_count  = 0,
         updated_at  = now()
    from _stale s
   where u.ticker = s.ticker
     and coalesce(u.is_delisted, false) = true
     and s.sessions_since < grace_sessions;
  get diagnostics n_restored = row_count;

  -- 3. Keep miss_count current for the rest, so the warning list below is readable.
  update universe u
     set miss_count = s.sessions_since
    from _stale s
   where u.ticker = s.ticker
     and coalesce(u.miss_count, -1) <> s.sessions_since;

  select count(*) into n_warning from _stale
   where sessions_since between 3 and grace_sessions - 1;
  select count(*) into n_missing from _del;

  raise notice 'retired %, restored %, % on warning (3-% sessions quiet), % in the loader''s missing list',
               n_retired, n_restored, n_warning, grace_sessions - 1, n_missing;
  raise notice 'price history is retained deliberately: delisted names are the part of the '
               'record the ranking model has never been able to learn from';
end $$;

COMMIT;

parameters.query:
select ticker, max(date_diff) as days_ago, exchange from (
select eu.*
, f.latest_filing
, f.latest_period
, case when f.latest_filing is null then eu.report_date - f.latest_period 
else eu.report_date - f.latest_filing 
	end as date_diff 
from earnings_upcoming eu 
left join (
	select ticker,
	       max(period_end)  as latest_period,
	       max(filing_date) as latest_filing,
	       max(as_of)       as latest_update      -- <<< added: newest fundamentals load
	from fundamentals_facts ff
	group by ticker) as f on f.ticker = eu.ticker
where eu.period_end != f.latest_period
and eu.report_date <= current_date - interval '1 days'
and (f.latest_update is null or f.latest_update::date <> current_date)   -- <<< added: skip if already updated today
AND EXISTS (
                         SELECT 1 FROM universe u
                         WHERE u.ticker = eu.ticker
                         and u.industry != 'Shell Companies') 
and case when f.latest_filing is null then eu.report_date - f.latest_period 
else eu.report_date - f.latest_filing 
	end >0) as summary
group by summary.ticker, summary.exchange
having max(date_diff) > 90 and max(date_diff) < 365
order by ticker asc;

parameters.query:
with daily as (
  select dp.date, count(*) as loaded
  from daily_prices dp
  join universe u on u.ticker = dp.ticker and u.type = 'Common Stock'
  where dp.date >= current_date - 30
  group by dp.date
),
latest as (select max(date) as d from daily),
base as (                                   -- median of the 10 days BEFORE the one being checked
  select (percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by loaded))::numeric as med
  from (select loaded from daily, latest where date < latest.d order by date desc limit 10) z
),
cur as (select loaded from daily, latest where date = latest.d)
select l.d                                             as load_date,
       c.loaded,
       round(b.med)                                    as baseline,
       round(c.loaded::numeric / nullif(b.med, 0), 3)  as ratio,
       case
         when l.d < (current_date - case when extract(dow from current_date) = 1 then 3 else 1 end) then 'STALE'
         when c.loaded::numeric / nullif(b.med, 0) < 0.97 then 'PARTIAL'
         else 'OK'
       end                                             as verdict
from latest l, base b, cur c;
